Un homme survécut à la tuerie : Ofusu Kingsley Cudjoe. Du Ghana à l'Ukraine, le journaliste du quotidien Le Monde, Philippe Broussard, a reconstitué l'histoire de ce drame. Son enquête fait l'objet d'un album de bande dessinée, L’Odyssée tragique du MC Ruby, publié aux éditions Dupuis.

items.title: ‘Capturing Bigfoot’ Review: An Astounding Documentary Uncovers the Truth
items.summary: "Capturing Bigfoot" is an amazing documentary about the legend of Bigfoot — about how it was born, how it took hold, and how that iconic piece of film footage came to be. It’s a documentary that answers all the questions and solves all the mysteries. Unlike your typical film about UFOs, it doesn’t leave you with that vague feeling of "The truth is still out there, and I’m not sure what it is." items.summary: arXiv:2610.20667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid advances in AI capabilities are causing benchmarks to saturate. items.summary: arXiv:2610.20675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents pair reasoning models with harnesses that organize model calls, execute tools, load skill instructions, and retain history in memory. items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security
items.summary: During the Syrian war (2011–24), the Assad Government forces and their Russian allies conducted hundreds of strikes on medical facilities in opposition-held areas. Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia

In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. However, Pepe's symptoms slowly worsened and 10 weeks later he returned to the physician, who ordered a gastroscopy, which occurred 2 months later, revealing an ulcerated mass.

items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
items.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
